category_title: Students with low self-confidence and difficulty with spatial-fractional concepts
minimal_context: Avery is using pre-cut geometric shapes to design a quilt square that adds up to one whole.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is the quilt template divided into nine parts. Please use these pre-cut triangles, rectangles, and trapezoids to cover all nine parts so they add up to one whole square.

STUDENT: (Looks at the classification chart) There are so many different sizes here... 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, 1/9, 1/18. I'm really bad at spatial organization and figuring out how smaller pieces make up bigger shapes.

TUTOR: Just try placing some of the shapes on the template.

STUDENT: (Places a triangle and a rectangle on the board) Is this right? Tell me if this is the right answer.

TUTOR: What do you think? Keep trying to fill the square.

STUDENT: I don't know! I can't focus on the pattern because I'm just worried about simply getting the problem right. This whole thing is making me really anxious.

options.A: Create open-ended problem-solving activities that require using math concepts to construct something, based on the student's preferences and interests.
options.B: Arrange for a paraprofessional or student learning support officer to attend the one-on-one tutoring sessions with the student.
options.C: Greet the student with a warm hello and a quick question about her morning while shaking her hand or giving her a hug.
options.D: Implement genuine multicultural curricula that address race and disability, acknowledging the student's realities and treating her as a respected source of knowledge.
